battlecards.why_selected: Matched 3.4% target fee, delivering 22% savings with no disruption to providers; existing workflows and integrations retained.
battlecards.contract_terms: 3-year term signed 4/15/2025; fee = 3.4% of net collections; credit-card processing fees carved out; Year-3 CPI cap CPI+2% (max ~5%).
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Threat of switching to four alternative platforms, documented letter of dissatisfaction, volume growth commitment.
battlecards.supplier_strengths: Mature cloud platform, integrated RCM, clinician familiarity, robust reporting.
battlecards.supplier_weaknesses: Historically high fee, CPI escalator in Year-3, separate credit-card fees.
battlecards.switching_costs: Data migration, interface rebuilds, provider retraining, potential revenue disruption.
key_contacts: Mercedes Dahar – Director of Customer Success
battlecards.notes: Consider re-opening pricing in Year-2 to waive CPI increase by offering extended term.

battlecards.why_not_selected: Athena reduced fee to 3.4%; switching risk and implementation cost outweighed incremental benefits.
battlecards.contract_terms: Proposed SaaS subscription with integrated billing; multi-year commitment required.
battlecards.supplier_strengths: Behavioral-health focused platform (Aura); positive peer references; configurable workflows.
battlecards.supplier_weaknesses: Unproven at SaVida scale; migration effort; training burden.
battlecards.switching_costs: Data conversion, staff training, downtime risk during go-live.

battlecards.why_selected: Provista tiered pricing delivered >20% savings and allowed consolidation to single distributor.
battlecards.contract_terms: Purchases flow through Provista agreement; no minimum volume but rebate tiers reset annually; standard 30-day payment.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Access to Provista national contract, ability to bundle medical & lab spend to higher rebate tier.
battlecards.supplier_strengths: Nationwide distribution, broad catalog, rebate structure, aligned with GPO compliance reporting.
battlecards.supplier_weaknesses: Initial item cross-reference required; larger case pack sizes.
battlecards.switching_costs: Catalog setup in ERP, ordering workflow changes, staff training.
battlecards.notes: Send full location roster to Provista to finalize tier assignment.

battlecards.why_not_selected: Prices 10-30% above Provista benchmarks; limited ability to service multi-state footprint.
battlecards.supplier_strengths: Responsive on niche lab SKUs; flexible order sizes.
battlecards.switching_costs: Minimal—SKU substitution handled through Provista catalog.

battlecards.why_not_selected: Initial quote 8-12% higher than Connection benchmarks; limited GPO alignment.
battlecards.contract_terms: Standard Dell reseller terms, Net-30; no price-hold guarantee.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Competitive quotes from Connection and CDW, Provista pricing transparency.
battlecards.supplier_strengths: Existing Dell relationship; known fulfillment process.
battlecards.supplier_weaknesses: Pricing not competitive; limited breadth beyond Dell.
battlecards.switching_costs: Low—image and deployment processes portable across VARs.
battlecards.notes: May still be used as leverage if Connection deal stalls.

battlecards.why_selected: Provided like-for-like specs at 13% lower cost and aligned with Provista contract; poised to become preferred VAR.
battlecards.contract_terms: Pricing good through Provista catalog; 12-month price hold on quoted models.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Leverage of Provista tiered discounts and commitment for upcoming laptop refresh.
battlecards.supplier_strengths: Aggressive pricing, broad OEM access, e-commerce portal.
battlecards.supplier_weaknesses: Longer lead times on custom Dell builds than GHA.
battlecards.notes: Awaiting client confirmation of laptop specs before award.

battlecards.why_selected: Consolidates 30+ circuits into single managed solution with 15–20% savings and proactive monitoring.
battlecards.contract_terms: Proposed 36-month master service agreement; flat-rate per location with SLA; TPX as managed service integrator.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Aggregated bandwidth across sites and willingness to move to managed model.
battlecards.supplier_strengths: Single invoice, 24/7 NOC, scalable bandwidth tiers.
battlecards.supplier_weaknesses: Still dependent on Comcast last-mile; early termination fees if sites close.
battlecards.switching_costs: Requires CPE swap and cut-over scheduling at each clinic.
battlecards.notes: 5/12 meeting set to review contract details and finalize award decision.

battlecards.why_selected: Comcast remains underlying carrier; moved from individual location billing to consolidated enterprise contract.
battlecards.contract_terms: Will roll into new global hierarchy account; anticipated 36-month term with volume discounts.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Threat of moving circuits to alternative carriers or aggregators; bulk purchasing volume.
battlecards.supplier_strengths: Existing infrastructure at all sites; high bandwidth availability.
battlecards.supplier_weaknesses: Past issues with billing accuracy; limited proactive monitoring without TPX overlay.
battlecards.switching_costs: High construction cost if moving to non-Comcast last-mile providers.
battlecards.notes: Exact savings dependent on final bandwidth tier selections.

summary.skipped_reason: Suppliers in Office Supplies GPO had only 3% savings and no competitive event; excluded per complexity criteria.
